test.name: Spec 0010 spike: PROC_PIDTBSDINFO on other users' processes

expected: inspect can read the start time and uid of a pid that now belongs to another user, so a reused recorded pid classifies as gone (pid_reused) when instance.lock is free, not as unproven (spec 0010 AC-10, Adapter macOS row Waktu start, user, group, parent, tertahan)
actual: PROC_PIDTBSDINFO returns EPERM for every process of another user that still existed (168 of 168, root daemons and _-users; pid 1 too), and PROC_PIDLISTFDS returns EPERM for them as well. With the row's method alone, inspect for a recorded pid that the system reused for another user's process fails with PermissionDenied, and spec 0010 classifies any evidence error as Unproven (identityUnproven) instead of Gone(pid_reused), so the instance would stay unknown until that unrelated process exits. What works: sysctl {CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, pid} returned kinfo_proc with uid (kp_eproc.e_ucred.cr_uid, offset 420) and start time (kp_proc.p_starttime, offsets 0 and 8) for 168 of 168 of them, equal to PROC_PIDTBSDINFO for our own process; proc_pidpath and getsid also work for them. libc 0.2.190 has no Apple kinfo_proc, so the adapter would declare it (size 648). Spec 0010 needs a decision here (adapter falls back to kinfo_proc for uid and start time, or the spec accepts Unproven for this case).
